correctness.rationale: All 8192 binary words length thirteen are exhaustively partitioned by exact one-gap 1/2/3 deck integer tuples; every length-13 word has the same tuple under two independent algorithms, direct index-subset enumeration and a last-selected-index dynamic programming recurrence. Exactly four explicit reversed doubletons occur. Direct computation also verifies equality of three punctured 2-decks for each pair and the failure of punctured 3-deck equality. The arbitrary-context theorem follows for ALL contexts from a proof partitioning deck selections by their exact exterior indices and using the relevant intact/punctured decks. Independent block switches then yield 2^m distinct words for ALL m. 8188 maximum code size and 16 codebooks follow exactly from the observed 8184 singleton/four doubleton partition; reversal/complement fixed counts 16,0,4,4 give 6 orbits via Burnside. Finite checks do not substitute for arbitrary-length proofs.

originality.rationale: Primary full texts distinguish published G(3)=13 and one example from the new complete four-class census and the stronger arbitrary-context 3-deck substitution. The 2022 padded higher-k construction requires full k-puncture equality and does not imply the present weaker 2-puncture all-context lemma for these four pairs; direct tests show its stronger premise fails. The 2023 local rewrites concern k=2 and explicitly explain noncongruence for positive gaps. The standard ungapped deck census concerns a different statistic. Searches of the available indexed records and accessible prior claims found no statement covering both the complete length-13 four-doubleton classification and the unpadded length-3 context lemma. Possible unindexed equivalents remain a stated risk.

value.rationale: The new result resolves the entire first nongeneric ambiguity class partition of the natural one-gap three-subsequence reconstruction channel, determines every maximum 13-bit reconstruction codebook, and proves a nontrivial, unpadded two-sided local-substitution principle in a relation known not to be a general congruence. The substitution theorem has a measurable consequence beyond a first counterexample: indistinguishability classes grow to at least 2^m at length 13m, giving a reusable lower-bound family of channel ambiguities. A finite table alone would be limited; the infinite structural lemma and codebook structure make the exact data mathematically motivated.
